questions.text: Mandatory : No Calculator : None Response Time : N.A Think Time : N.A Minimum Instruction Time : 0 You work as a product designer for a company that manufactures mobile phones. The latest model of the phone has been receiving complaints from customers about poor battery life. Your manager has asked you to investigate the issue and come up with a solution. You decide to use Multi-why Analysis and Design Thinking to approach the problem. You ask "Why" questions to identify the root cause of the battery life issue. Which of the following is an example of a "Why" question you might ask?
options: Why do customers dislike the phone's design?
Why do other phones have better battery life?
Why is the phone's battery draining quickly?
Why is the phone's camera not functioning properly?
questions.correct_answer: Why is the phone's battery draining quickly?

questions.text: Mandatory : No Calculator : None Response Time : N.A Think Time : N.A Minimum Instruction Time : 0 Which of the following best describes natural mapping in the context of stove burners according to human factors in design principles?
options: The placement of controls as far away as possible from the object to be controlled.
The arrangement of controls around the object to be controlled by nature.
The use of a separate room for controls away from the object to be controlled.
The use of spatial cues to create a direct relationship between the controls and the object to be controlled.
questions.correct_answer: The use of spatial cues to create a direct relationship between the controls and the object to be controlled.

Mandatory : No Calculator : None Response Time : N.A Think Time : N.A Minimum Instruction Time : 0 In a design thinking context, a conflict of interest may arise when a designer must balance the needs and desires of multiple stakeholders. Which of the following approaches could be used to resolve this conflict?
options: Prioritizing the needs of the most powerful stakeholder.
Negotiating a compromise that satisfies all stakeholders to some degree.
Ignoring the conflict and focusing solely on the needs of the end user.
Outsourcing the decision-making process to a third party.
questions.correct_answer: Negotiating a compromise that satisfies all stakeholders to some degree.

questions.text: Mandatory : No Calculator : None Response Time : N.A Think Time : N.A Minimum Instruction Time : 0 How did design thinking play a role in the construction of the Shivanasamudram Falls power plant?
options: By allowing the engineers to use the latest technologies and construction methods.
By encouraging the engineers to consider the needs and perspectives of the local communities.
By ensuring that the power plant was built as quickly and efficiently as possible.
By prioritizing cost savings and minimizing the use of expensive materials.
questions.correct_answer: By encouraging the engineers to consider the needs and perspectives of the local communities.

questions.text: Mandatory : No Calculator : None Response Time : N.A Think Time : N.A Minimum Instruction Time : 0 What role did serendipity play in Joseph Monier's development of reinforced concrete?
options: He was inspired by the shapes and textures of the natural world.
He accidentally stumbled upon the idea while working on a different project.
He conducted extensive market research to identify new opportunities for construction materials.
He was able to leverage existing technologies and materials to create a new product.
questions.correct_answer: He accidentally stumbled upon the idea while working on a different project.

questions.text: Mandatory : No Calculator : None Response Time : N.A Think Time : N.A Minimum Instruction Time : 0 Which of the following best describes the transition from trial and error to a more systematic approach to innovation?
options: A shift from intuition and luck to data and analysis.
A move away from creativity and imagination towards rigid rules and procedures.
An abandonment of experimentation and iteration in favor of pre-determined solutions.
A focus on serendipity and chance discoveries rather than deliberate problem- solving.
questions.correct_answer: A shift from intuition and luck to data and analysis.

questions.text: Mandatory : No Calculator : None Response Time : N.A Think Time : N.A Minimum Instruction Time : 0 What is the main advantage of a more systematic approach to innovation?
options: It allows for more creativity and imagination in the design process.
It enables faster iteration and testing of new ideas.
It relies on a trial-and-error approach to solve complex problems.
It reduces the risk of failure and increases the likelihood of success.
questions.correct_answer: It reduces the risk of failure and increases the likelihood of success.

questions.text: Mandatory : No Calculator : None Response Time : N.A Think Time : N.A Minimum Instruction Time : 0 Recalling the interaction between Mr. Venkatakrishnan Janakiraman and Prof. Bala Ramadurai, what according to Mr. Janakiraman was a major conflict of interest associated with getting into the details when building a business?
options: It can be easy to lose sight of the bigger picture and get bogged down in day- to-day operations.
It can be difficult to delegate tasks effectively and manage a team when you are overly focused on the details.
It can be challenging to identify and prioritize which details are most important to focus on.
It can be difficult to communicate the importance of details to stakeholders and team members who are focused on the bigger picture
questions.correct_answer: It can be easy to lose sight of the bigger picture and get bogged down in day- to-day operations.
